claim_verdicts.evidence: tools/extract-code at stage-3: DonHang.Domain/OrderMessage.cs, DonHang.Notifications/OrderMessage.cs and DonHang.Payments/Messages.cs each declare `public sealed record OrderMessage(int OrderId, string CustomerEmail, string CustomerName, DateTimeOffset OccurredAt);`. Notifications' comment: "This service keeps its own copy of the shape instead of referencing DonHang.Domain".

envs/production/kustomization.yaml @ stage-3, `images:` has six entries (donhang-api, donhang-migrate, donhang-notifications, donhang-notifications-migrate, donhang-payments, donhang-payments-migrate), each with its own newTag and digest; all six newTag = sha-25158b4d4f7cb9a5c0b944f5ea8482221a24b4be.

Round 2. base/db.yaml: one StatefulSet `db` (postgres:17.6-alpine). base/db-backup.yaml lines 53-54: `for db in donhang donhang_notifications donhang_payments; do pg_dump -Fc -h db -U donhang -d "$db" ...`. The claim now names the backup CronJob, and Try it answer 3 says it must learn the new server.
Definitional framing of the anti-pattern taken from outline items 1-2; the lesson presents it as the lesson's checklist, not as a cited fact about a product.

DonHang.Domain/OrderService.cs @ stage-3 lines 43-50: "Its handlers add their rows (an outbox message, say) to the same DbContext first; this one SaveChangesAsync then writes the order and those rows in one transaction". The API never calls Notifications; OrderEventsConsumer consumes the queue with autoAck: false. Placing an order waits on no consumer.

Round 2. OrdersController.cs: `return Accepted(ToDto(order));`. RefundRequestedConsumer.HandleAsync comment: "Nothing calls the gateway here; that is RefundSender's job, a moment later". RefundSender.cs line 58: `gateway.RefundAsync(refund, stoppingToken)`. GatewayRefundClient.cs: "Where the payment gateway is and the key it gives Đơn Hàng"; the lesson's "payment provider" is a fair plain rendering.

ProjectReference @ stage-3: Api -> Domain, Infrastructure, Catalog, Messaging; Infrastructure -> Domain, Catalog, Messaging; Notifications -> Messaging only; Payments -> Messaging only. ModuleBoundaryTests.MessagingUsesNoDonHangProject asserts DonHang.Messaging references no DonHang.* assembly.

Round 2. PostgreSQL 17 docs: "A database cluster is a collection of databases that is managed by a single instance of a running database server." Lesson now says the server stopping "takes all three databases down at once, and every service's work that needs its database fails together"; the consumers nack and requeue failed work (`BasicNackAsync(..., requeue: true)`).

Kubernetes docs, kustomization fields table: "images | ... | Each entry is to modify the name, tags and/or digest for one image without creating patches". ci.yml @ stage-3: publish job matrix lists the six images and pushes each as `$name:sha-$GITHUB_SHA` (lines 211-256), so one commit yields all six.

Round 3. Section 5 now says both readers reject a message whose CustomerEmail is missing. Both Read() call `JsonSerializer.Deserialize<OrderMessage>(body, JsonSerializerOptions.Web)` and throw PoisonMessageException when `string.IsNullOrEmpty(message.CustomerEmail)` (RefundRequestedConsumer.cs line 126; OrderEventsConsumer.cs line 133). .NET docs: "A missing property doesn't throw an exception, even for non-nullable properties".

Round 3. ModuleBoundaryTests.cs @ stage-3 lines 56-72 match the block verbatim. Prose line refs now in the block's numbering: line 64 = `var referenced = ...GetReferencedAssemblies()`, lines 60-61 = the two [InlineData], line 72 = the DonHang.Messaging comment. `.Where(name => name.StartsWith("DonHang.") && name != "DonHang.Messaging")` then `Assert.Empty(referenced)`: a DonHang.Shared reference would fail.

Round 2. Row 1 now reads "yes, but every service's next build carries every change to `Order`, used or not", consistent with section 4 and ci.yml (all six images built per commit, each promotable alone). What remains is a comparative judgement with its costs stated, not a product fact.

Conditional recommendations ("unless...", "if one does..."), stated as choices with their conditions. Section 7's factual sentence now reads "would reach all three in their next build", consistent with claim 12.

Definitional: a container places a process; it says nothing about code or release dependencies. Round 3 targeted re-check found no issues; opened: lesson sections 4, 5, 9; tools/extract-code ModuleBoundaryTests.cs 56-72 and DonHang.Payments/Messages.cs @ stage-3; RefundRequestedConsumer.cs and OrderEventsConsumer.cs @ stage-3; meta claims 10-13.

issues.text: Carried from round 2, narrowed again. Explanation d no longer says the lesson weighs joint releases against merging back, but it now says joint releases are "what is left" when no move works. Section 7 says the opposite path: if no move works, the split may not pay for itself and the next question is merging back. I cannot find "living with joint releases" anywhere in the lesson.
issues.quote: Joint releases are what is left only when no move of the knowledge removes the change in step, and the lesson asks that question first.
issues.fix: Replace the last sentence of explanation d with "The lesson asks first whether moving the knowledge removes the change in step." Update vi to match.
